title: PMSM FOC vs. FEC — Thrust Dynamometer Comparison
author: Helmon Filipe Alexandre Manjate
publisher: Project repository for an MSc thesis, Poznań University of Technology
status: File-level evidence, author-curated plotted numeric series, embedded JSON decoded
rights: Repository MIT license names the software and associated documentation. This package links to the dashboards and contributes original aggregates. A separate raw-series license is not given.
input_mapping: Steady series contain commanded duty in percent and drive telemetry. The transient labels describe steps from 20% to 30%, 60% or 80%. The firmware's steady profile rate-limits current_throttle towards target_throttle, while the transient step itself is assigned immediately. The plotted release lacks two simultaneous columns for pre- and post-limit values.
endpoints: An ESP32 muxes controller bus voltage/current and RPM with an HX711 load cell on a lever arm. The load-cell channel reports thrust in the author's grams scale. The firmware's Torque(Nm) channel is computed from phase current and Kt; for the Vertiq it estimates phase current from bus current divided by commanded duty. The output shaft has no independently instrumented torque channel here.
method: The merged HTML contains JSON constants D (Vertiq FEC) and F (VESC FOC). The standalone FEC report duplicates D byte-for-byte at the JSON data level after parsing and serialization. Keep it once. Count only finite steady rows, retain all displayed repetitions, and use distinct time arrays bms and thr_t for controller and force data. Produce trial and group summaries on the published display arrays. The <12 V threshold is an audit threshold, not the configured limiter.
findings: There are 5,556 complete FEC steady samples and 3 aligned null separators in 5,559 slots. Six 19-level sweep summaries are present across both drives. Nineteen transients contain 4,226 bus samples and 396 displayed force samples.

All five displayed samples below 12 V occur in the three FEC 20→80% repetitions. The minimum is 10.57 V; peak current is 17.36 A. In repetition 3, 249 electrical points accompany one displayed load-cell point at 7.8 ms, −0.6 g. That trace cannot yield a force rise time.

The dashboard explicitly labels the 80% FEC speed rise time as supply-limited and reports a corrected digit-drop glitch in force. It states that discarding the low FEC sweep 2 shifted the merged comparison. The published FEC steady and efficiency objects retain sweeps 1, 3 and 4.
limitations: The two controllers use different physical motors, a common propeller and different UART polling rates. A drive-architecture-only causal contrast cannot be isolated.

The setup guide leaves calibration reference-mass value, configured VESC current limits and select regen limit settings as outstanding. Voltage sag and current peaks in the published arrays cannot reconstruct internal unclipped commands.
Transient force updates are sparse compared with motor telemetry. Embedded series were processed for display and contain an explicit corrected glitch. Raw CSV acquisition files were not used here.
queries: GitHub repository search: motor dynamometer load cell csv in:readme
Read pinned README, LICENSE, guide, firmware and both HTML results. Compare both embedded FEC objects and inspect all retained transients.
reproducibility: node derive-manjate.mjs OUT [LOCAL_DASHBOARD_DIRECTORY] verifies both Git blob objects and regenerates four tables.
